ABOUT UMRAH CONNECT
The connected operating system for Umrah.

We replace the spreadsheets, group chats, paper registers and disconnected tools the Umrah industry relies on today — with one calm, structured, connected platform.

Our mission

Pilgrims travel for Umrah with support from operators, hotels, transport companies and visa agencies that still coordinate over spreadsheets and messaging apps. Umrah Connect brings them together into a single role-based operating system — a marketplace, CRM, booking engine, social hub and finance ledger that lets every stakeholder do their best work while giving pilgrims a clear, trusted journey.

7

Connected roles

Service first

Every feature is built to make the pilgrim journey calmer and the operator’s work lighter.

Trust & compliance

Provider review, workspace governance and recorded operational activity.

One connected ecosystem

Travelers, operators, hotels, transport, visa and finance working on the same trusted data.

Purpose-built

Designed specifically for Umrah and Hajj — not a generic tool bent to fit.

LEGAL

Privacy Policy

Last updated: June 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Umrah Connect collects, uses and protects information across our platform — for travelers, operators, hotels, transport companies, visa agencies and finance teams.

1. Information we collect

We collect information you provide when you create an account, complete bookings, submit website forms, or contact us — such as your name, email, phone number, organization and travel details. For providers, we also collect business and KYC verification information.

2. How we use your information

We use your information to operate the platform: to process bookings and payments, coordinate between travelers and providers, verify provider identity, send notifications, provide support, and improve our services. Operator and pilgrim data is scoped to its tenant.

3. Data sharing

We share booking and coordination data only with the providers and operators directly involved in your journey. We do not sell your personal information. Service providers who help us run the platform are bound by confidentiality obligations.

4. Data security

We protect your data with encrypted authentication, role-based access control, multi-tenant isolation and audit logging. Access to your data is restricted to your role and tenant.

5. Data retention

We retain your information for as long as your account is active or as needed to provide services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes and enforce agreements.

6. Your rights

You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, subject to legal and operational requirements. Contact us to exercise these rights.

7. Contact

For privacy questions or requests, contact us through the Contact page. We will respond as promptly as we can.

SECURITY & TRUST
Built for trust and protection.

Umrah Connect handles pilgrim data, payments and operator records — security and compliance are foundational, not afterthoughts.

Account authentication

JWT-based sessions with short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt.

Role-based access control

Account roles and endpoint permissions determine supported actions. Workspace context is visible in the application.

Tenant workspaces

Workspaces organize tenant records separately. Access is controlled by the platform and account permissions.

Audit logging

Governance screens provide recorded activity with actor, action and timestamp where supported.

KYC verification

Governance includes a provider KYC review workflow. Review the specific provider and service information before booking.

Application controls

Hardened HTTP headers, input validation and upload controls form part of the platform implementation.

Questions about security or compliance?

Our team is happy to walk through how Umrah Connect protects your data.

By accessing or using Umrah Connect, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you are using the platform on behalf of an organization, you agree on its behalf.

HOW UMRAH CONNECT WORKS
Simple. Smart. Seamless.

Explore the supported service paths. Inquiry, request, booking and payment actions vary by service and workspace.

STEP 1

Search

Browse published hotel, transport, visa and package listings. Check the provider information on each service.

STEP 2

Compare

Review price, location, inclusions and available review information on each listing. Confirm availability with the provider.

STEP 3

Request / Book

Send a request or book directly. Operators receive your enquiry and respond with quotations and offers.

STEP 4

Review Confirmation

Review the service, dates, party size and supported price estimate. Nightly and custom rates require a provider inquiry.

STEP 5

Payment / Invoice

Use the payment options enabled for your invoice. Recorded payments, outstanding balances and booking status are separate.

STEP 6

Notifications

Read the notifications generated by supported platform actions in your account.

STEP 7

Travel Management

View your marketplace bookings and requests. Ask your operator for group itineraries and personal visa updates.

STEP 8

Provider Coordination

Provider workspaces organize their respective booking, inventory, assignment and application records.

TRAVEL GUIDANCE
Best times to visit the Rawdah in Madinah

4 min read · Umrah Connect team

The Rawdah ash-Sharifah — the area between the Prophet’s ﷺ minbar and his blessed home — is one of the most sought-after places on earth. A little planning makes the visit calmer and more likely to succeed.

Book through Nusuk first

Entry to the Rawdah is organised through timed permits booked in the official Nusuk app. Permits are free but limited; slots open on a rolling basis, so check the app daily and book as soon as your travel dates are confirmed.

Men and women have separate visiting hours and entrances — check which window your permit falls into and arrive early for it.

The calmest windows

Late night (after Isha crowds disperse, roughly 11pm–2am) and the period after Fajr are usually the most settled times. Between Dhuhr and Asr is often quieter than the evening rush.

Fridays, the last ten nights of Ramadan and Hajj season are the busiest — if your trip allows, plan your Rawdah visit for a mid-week day outside peak season.

On the day

Arrive at the gate printed on your permit at least 20–30 minutes early, keep your Nusuk QR code ready offline, and travel light — large bags slow down entry.

Once inside, time is short. Prioritise two rak‘ahs and your most important du‘ās rather than photography; guards keep the flow moving.

For operators

If you manage groups, collect your pilgrims’ Nusuk accounts early and coordinate permit slots per group. Staggering sub-groups across windows works better than pushing one large block into a single slot.

ABOUT UMRAH CONNECT
The connected operating system for Umrah.

We replace the spreadsheets, group chats, paper registers and disconnected tools the Umrah industry relies on today — with one calm, structured, connected platform.

LEGAL

Privacy Policy

Last updated: June 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Umrah Connect collects, uses and protects information across our platform — for travelers, operators, hotels, transport companies, visa agencies and finance teams.

1. Information we collect

We collect information you provide when you create an account, complete bookings, submit website forms, or contact us — such as your name, email, phone number, organization and travel details. For providers, we also collect business and KYC verification information.

2. How we use your information

We use your information to operate the platform: to process bookings and payments, coordinate between travelers and providers, verify provider identity, send notifications, provide support, and improve our services. Operator and pilgrim data is scoped to its tenant.

3. Data sharing

We share booking and coordination data only with the providers and operators directly involved in your journey. We do not sell your personal information. Service providers who help us run the platform are bound by confidentiality obligations.

4. Data security

We protect your data with encrypted authentication, role-based access control, multi-tenant isolation and audit logging. Access to your data is restricted to your role and tenant.

5. Data retention

We retain your information for as long as your account is active or as needed to provide services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes and enforce agreements.

6. Your rights

You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, subject to legal and operational requirements. Contact us to exercise these rights.

7. Contact

For privacy questions or requests, contact us through the Contact page. We will respond as promptly as we can.

SECURITY & TRUST
Built for trust and protection.

Umrah Connect handles pilgrim data, payments and operator records — security and compliance are foundational, not afterthoughts.

Account authentication

JWT-based sessions with short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt.

Role-based access control

Account roles and endpoint permissions determine supported actions. Workspace context is visible in the application.

Tenant workspaces

Workspaces organize tenant records separately. Access is controlled by the platform and account permissions.

Audit logging

Governance screens provide recorded activity with actor, action and timestamp where supported.

KYC verification

Governance includes a provider KYC review workflow. Review the specific provider and service information before booking.

Application controls

Hardened HTTP headers, input validation and upload controls form part of the platform implementation.

Questions about security or compliance?

Our team is happy to walk through how Umrah Connect protects your data.

SOLUTIONS FOR EVERY ROLE
One platform, seven dedicated solutions.

Umrah Connect gives every part of the Umrah ecosystem its own purpose-built workspace — connected to the same trusted data.

TRAVELERS / PILGRIMS

Plan, book and manage your sacred journey with confidence.

Browse and compare verified hotels, transport, visa and full packages
Track bookings, itinerary, departures and visa status in one place
Join the Social Hub community, groups and trusted provider updates
Receive real-time notifications for confirmations, payments and travel updates

OPERATORS / AGENCIES

Run your entire Umrah operation from one connected workspace.

Pilgrim CRM with profiles, passports, group assignments and audit trail
Bookings pipeline from inquiry to quotation to confirmation
Hotel allotments, transport assignments and visa compliance in one view
Finance snapshot: revenue, receipts, payables and reconciliation

HOTELS / ACCOMMODATION

Optimize occupancy, pricing and the guest experience.

Room inventory, allotments and live availability by room type
Occupancy, RevPAR and average daily rate analytics
Booking status tracking and guest experience feedback
List your property on the Umrah Connect marketplace

TRANSPORT / LOGISTICS

Smart routing, fleet management and real-time coordination.

Manage vehicles, drivers and routes per group and departure
Assign transport to bookings and track on-time performance
Coordinate airport, Makkah and Madinah transfers
Fleet utilization and trip analytics

VISA SERVICES

A clear workspace for visa applications and documents.

Application pipeline and document checklist; official connectors are on the roadmap
Track submission, review, approval and rejection statuses
Manage applicant documents and service requests
Compliance reporting and approval-rate analytics

FINANCE / PAYMENTS

Reconciliation, settlements and financial insight, SAR-native.

Quotes → invoices → payments → reconciliation in one ledger
Record payments, partial payments and refunds with full history
Budget plans and outstanding-balance tracking
Financial reports and exportable analytics

SUPER ADMIN / GOVERNANCE

Platform-wide control, moderation and governance.

Manage all tenants, users, pilgrims, bookings and groups
KYC verification: review, approve and reject submissions
Marketplace moderation and listing approvals
Roles, permissions, audit logs and platform settings

Terms of Service

Last updated: June 2026

1. Acceptance of terms

By accessing or using Umrah Connect, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you are using the platform on behalf of an organization, you agree on its behalf.

2. The platform

Umrah Connect is a connected operating system for Umrah travel — a marketplace, CRM, booking engine, social hub and finance platform serving travelers, operators, hotels, transport companies, visa agencies and finance teams.

3. Accounts & roles

You are responsible for the accuracy of your account information and for safeguarding your credentials. Access is role-based and scoped to your tenant. Providers must complete KYC verification before transacting.

4. Bookings & providers

Bookings are agreements between travelers and the relevant providers. Umrah Connect facilitates discovery, coordination, payment and record-keeping, but providers are responsible for delivering their services.

5. Payments

Payments, invoices and refunds are processed and recorded on the platform in SAR. You agree to pay applicable amounts for services you book or provide.

6. Acceptable use

You agree not to misuse the platform, post unlawful or harmful content, attempt to access data outside your role, or disrupt the service. We may suspend accounts that violate these terms.

7. Content & community

Content you post to the Social Hub must respect community standards. You retain ownership of your content and grant us a license to display it on the platform.

8. Limitation of liability

The platform is provided on an "as is" basis. To the extent permitted by law, Umrah Connect is not liable for indirect or consequential damages arising from your use of the service.

9. Changes

We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of the platform after changes constitutes acceptance of the updated terms.

10. Contact

Questions about these terms can be sent through the Contact page.

HOW UMRAH CONNECT WORKS
Simple. Smart. Seamless.

Explore the supported service paths. Inquiry, request, booking and payment actions vary by service and workspace.

STEP 1

Search

Browse published hotel, transport, visa and package listings. Check the provider information on each service.

STEP 2

Compare

Review price, location, inclusions and available review information on each listing. Confirm availability with the provider.

STEP 3

Request / Book

Send a request or book directly. Operators receive your enquiry and respond with quotations and offers.

STEP 4

Review Confirmation

Review the service, dates, party size and supported price estimate. Nightly and custom rates require a provider inquiry.

STEP 5

Payment / Invoice

Use the payment options enabled for your invoice. Recorded payments, outstanding balances and booking status are separate.

STEP 6

Notifications

Read the notifications generated by supported platform actions in your account.

STEP 7

Travel Management

View your marketplace bookings and requests. Ask your operator for group itineraries and personal visa updates.

STEP 8

Provider Coordination

Provider workspaces organize their respective booking, inventory, assignment and application records.

TRAVEL GUIDANCE
Best times to visit the Rawdah in Madinah

4 min read · Umrah Connect team

The Rawdah ash-Sharifah — the area between the Prophet’s ﷺ minbar and his blessed home — is one of the most sought-after places on earth. A little planning makes the visit calmer and more likely to succeed.

Book through Nusuk first

Entry to the Rawdah is organised through timed permits booked in the official Nusuk app. Permits are free but limited; slots open on a rolling basis, so check the app daily and book as soon as your travel dates are confirmed.

Men and women have separate visiting hours and entrances — check which window your permit falls into and arrive early for it.

The calmest windows

Late night (after Isha crowds disperse, roughly 11pm–2am) and the period after Fajr are usually the most settled times. Between Dhuhr and Asr is often quieter than the evening rush.

Fridays, the last ten nights of Ramadan and Hajj season are the busiest — if your trip allows, plan your Rawdah visit for a mid-week day outside peak season.

On the day

Arrive at the gate printed on your permit at least 20–30 minutes early, keep your Nusuk QR code ready offline, and travel light — large bags slow down entry.

Once inside, time is short. Prioritise two rak‘ahs and your most important du‘ās rather than photography; guards keep the flow moving.

For operators

If you manage groups, collect your pilgrims’ Nusuk accounts early and coordinate permit slots per group. Staggering sub-groups across windows works better than pushing one large block into a single slot.

CONNECTED JOURNEYS

ABOUT UMRAH CONNECT
The connected operating system for Umrah.

We replace the spreadsheets, group chats, paper registers and disconnected tools the Umrah industry relies on today — with one calm, structured, connected platform.

Our mission

Pilgrims travel for Umrah with support from operators, hotels, transport companies and visa agencies that still coordinate over spreadsheets and messaging apps. Umrah Connect brings them together into a single role-based operating system — a marketplace, CRM, booking engine, social hub and finance ledger that lets every stakeholder do their best work while giving pilgrims a clear, trusted journey.

Purpose-built

LEGAL

Privacy Policy

Last updated: June 2026

This Privacy Policy explains how Umrah Connect collects, uses and protects information across our platform — for travelers, operators, hotels, transport companies, visa agencies and finance teams.

1. Information we collect

We collect information you provide when you create an account, complete bookings, submit website forms, or contact us — such as your name, email, phone number, organization and travel details. For providers, we also collect business and KYC verification information.

2. How we use your information

We use your information to operate the platform: to process bookings and payments, coordinate between travelers and providers, verify provider identity, send notifications, provide support, and improve our services. Operator and pilgrim data is scoped to its tenant.

3. Data sharing

We share booking and coordination data only with the providers and operators directly involved in your journey. We do not sell your personal information. Service providers who help us run the platform are bound by confidentiality obligations.

4. Data security

We protect your data with encrypted authentication, role-based access control, multi-tenant isolation and audit logging. Access to your data is restricted to your role and tenant.

5. Data retention

We retain your information for as long as your account is active or as needed to provide services, comply with legal obligations, resolve disputes and enforce agreements.

6. Your rights

You may request access to, correction of, or deletion of your personal information, subject to legal and operational requirements. Contact us to exercise these rights.

7. Contact

For privacy questions or requests, contact us through the Contact page. We will respond as promptly as we can.

CONNECTED JOURNEYS

Get Started
SECURITY & TRUST
Built for trust and protection.

Umrah Connect handles pilgrim data, payments and operator records — security and compliance are foundational, not afterthoughts.

Account authentication

JWT-based sessions with short-lived access tokens and rotating refresh tokens. Passwords are hashed with bcrypt.

Role-based access control

Account roles and endpoint permissions determine supported actions. Workspace context is visible in the application.

Tenant workspaces

Workspaces organize tenant records separately. Access is controlled by the platform and account permissions.

Audit logging

Governance screens provide recorded activity with actor, action and timestamp where supported.

KYC verification

Governance includes a provider KYC review workflow. Review the specific provider and service information before booking.

Application controls

Hardened HTTP headers, input validation and upload controls form part of the platform implementation.

Questions about security or compliance?

Our team is happy to walk through how Umrah Connect protects your data.

HOW UMRAH CONNECT WORKS
Simple. Smart. Seamless.

Explore the supported service paths. Inquiry, request, booking and payment actions vary by service and workspace.

STEP 1

Search

Browse published hotel, transport, visa and package listings. Check the provider information on each service.

STEP 2

Compare

Review price, location, inclusions and available review information on each listing. Confirm availability with the provider.

STEP 3

Request / Book

Send a request or book directly. Operators receive your enquiry and respond with quotations and offers.

STEP 4

Review Confirmation

Review the service, dates, party size and supported price estimate. Nightly and custom rates require a provider inquiry.

STEP 5

Payment / Invoice

Use the payment options enabled for your invoice. Recorded payments, outstanding balances and booking status are separate.

STEP 6

Notifications

Read the notifications generated by supported platform actions in your account.

STEP 7

Travel Management

View your marketplace bookings and requests. Ask your operator for group itineraries and personal visa updates.

STEP 8

Provider Coordination

Provider workspaces organize their respective booking, inventory, assignment and application records.

TRAVEL GUIDANCE
Best times to visit the Rawdah in Madinah

4 min read · Umrah Connect team

The Rawdah ash-Sharifah — the area between the Prophet’s ﷺ minbar and his blessed home — is one of the most sought-after places on earth. A little planning makes the visit calmer and more likely to succeed.

Book through Nusuk first

Entry to the Rawdah is organised through timed permits booked in the official Nusuk app. Permits are free but limited; slots open on a rolling basis, so check the app daily and book as soon as your travel dates are confirmed.

Men and women have separate visiting hours and entrances — check which window your permit falls into and arrive early for it.

The calmest windows

Late night (after Isha crowds disperse, roughly 11pm–2am) and the period after Fajr are usually the most settled times. Between Dhuhr and Asr is often quieter than the evening rush.

Fridays, the last ten nights of Ramadan and Hajj season are the busiest — if your trip allows, plan your Rawdah visit for a mid-week day outside peak season.

On the day

Arrive at the gate printed on your permit at least 20–30 minutes early, keep your Nusuk QR code ready offline, and travel light — large bags slow down entry.

Once inside, time is short. Prioritise two rak‘ahs and your most important du‘ās rather than photography; guards keep the flow moving.

For operators

If you manage groups, collect your pilgrims’ Nusuk accounts early and coordinate permit slots per group. Staggering sub-groups across windows works better than pushing one large block into a single slot.
